newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan, HK plan post-handover economic talks.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan, HK plan post-handover economic talks.

text.p: Taiwan and Hong Kong business leaders plan a major conference to discuss economic links between the island and China-ruled Hong Kong, a Taiwan organiser said on Tuesday.

"The Taiwan-Hong Kong economic conference is held every year. This year we plan to meet in Taipei around October or November," Joseph Chen, deputy secretary-general of Taipei's Chinese National Federation of Industries, told Reuters.
The Hong Kong Chamber of Commerce would send a large business delegation to attend the conference, Chen said.
"Post-handover economic links between Taiwan and Hong Kong will certainly be the main issue of our discussion," Chen said.

Hong Kong, which returned to Beijing rule at midnight on Monday night, is an important transit point for more than $30 billion in investment that has poured into China from Taiwan since the easing of unofficial ties in the late 1980s.
Despite increasing intricate economic ties linking Hong Kong, Taiwan and China, Taipei still bans direct investment in the mainland or official contacts there.
Taiwan executives have expressed concerns over Taiwan-Hong Kong relations in the post-handover period, fearing Beijing might use them to squeeze Taipei for political concessions.

Beijing, which has viewed Taiwan as a rebel-held province since a 1949 civil war split them, said the return of Hong Kong, and Portuguese-run Macau in 1999 will leave Taiwan as the only territory still awaiting "reunification with the motherland".
